transcript.text: Mitsuri. The report from the village states that seven homes were destroyed by the force of your Love Breathing during the battle. You know our rules about civilian protection. Why did you act with such force?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oyakata-sama, I... I did not intend for such damage to occur. The demon was particularly strong, and I had to focus all my energy on subduing it. I apologize for the oversight and for not being able to contain the impact of myBreathing technique better.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mitsuri, I understand that demons do not fight fair, and some are indeed more formidable than others. But our priority, above all else, is the protection of human life and their livelihoods. Seven homes... that represents the stability and shelter for many families, now shattered. Did you consider the potential collateral damage as you deployed your technique? Or was your focus solely on the demon, to the exclusion of all else?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mitsuri, your sincerity is clear, and I appreciate your promise to improve. However, "failed to consider" is a phrase that weighs heavily when seven families are displaced. Our techniques are powerful, designed to eradicate demons, but with that power comes a profound responsibility. Was there no alternative? No adjustment that could have been made, even a slight one, to protect the structures around you? I need to understand the thought process, or lack thereof, in that critical moment. What was it that prevented you from mitigating the damage?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oyakata-sama, I... I was so consumed by the need to end the demon's reign of terror that I allowed my resolve to override my better judgment. There may have been an alternative, but in the heat of battle, I did not take the time to assess the surrounding area as I should have. This was a grave error on my part, and I am truly remorseful for the impact it has had on the villagers. I vow to never let my emotions cloud my judgment in such a critical manner again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Consumed by the need to end the demon's reign" is a noble sentiment, Mitsuri, one that I understand well. Yet, a Hashira's resolve must always be tempered by foresight and an unwavering commitment to the safety of those we protect. It is precisely in those moments of intense battle, when emotions run highest, that our training and discipline must shine through.

To say your emotions "clouded your judgment" suggests a loss of control, even if momentary. As a Hashira, you are expected to maintain that control, to be a beacon of strength and reason. How do you intend to ensure this does not happen again? What specific steps will you take to prevent such an oversight, even when facing the most terrifying of demons?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oyakata-sama, I humbly accept your words as a crucial lesson. To prevent such an incident from occurring again, I will implement several changes to my approach. First, I will slow down my breathing technique slightly at the start of each engagement to ensure I am fully aware of my surroundings. Second, I will consciously remind myself to consider the impact of my actions on the environment before fully committing to a technique. Third, I will increase my focus on real-world combat scenarios in training, with particular emphasis on containing damage. Lastly, I will seek out additional guidance from you and the other Hashira on managing intense combat situations while maintaining situational awareness.

Those are concrete steps, Mitsuri, and I am pleased to hear that you are not simply offering apologies, but actively seeking pathways to improvement. To consciously remind yourself and to slow your technique, even for a moment, to assess the environment, is precisely the kind of discipline I expect from a Hashira. Your commitment to incorporating this into your training is also commendable.

I trust you will uphold these new practices with the same dedication you show in battle. We will discuss your progress again after your next several missions.
